POSITION OVERVIEW
As a Senior Business Advisor, Strategy within BDC Advisory Services, you act as a senior strategic advisor to entrepreneurs and executive teams at pivotal moments of growth, transformation, and ownership transition. BDC is the only bank dedicated exclusively to Canadian entrepreneurs, and your work directly supports the long‑term success of small and medium‑sized businesses across Canada.
This position resides in Advisory Services (management consulting) and will serve Canadian Small and Medium Entrepreneurs through our consulting mandates. This is not a Financing role. The ideal candidate will have strong business strategy consulting experience with M&A (mergers and acquisitions) and PMI (post-merger integration) experience. The ideal candidate will have a vision for the future of business in an AI driven world and will have supported the consulting sales cycle and management of a portfolio of projects delivered by consultants.
CHALLENGES TO BE MET
Lead complex, high‑impact advisory mandates for entrepreneurs and senior leadership teams, focused on enterprise‑level strategic planning, growth acceleration, organizational effectiveness, and leadership decision‑making within SME and mid‑market environments.
Maintain full accountability for mandate outcomes across multiple concurrent engagements, ensuring delivery excellence related to scope, budget, timelines, risk management, and quality of deliverables.
Act as a trusted senior advisor during periods of ambiguity, transformation, and change, applying market insight, competitive analysis, and practical experience to guide high‑stakes decisions.
Contribute to the evolution of the Strategy Centre of Expertise by developing, refining, and scaling advisory solutions, tools, and methodologies aligned with emerging client needs and market trends.
Support business development and revenue growth by partnering with senior client managers on complex sales cycles, including executive‑level diagnostics, value articulation, and proposal development.
Enable strong internal collaboration by connecting advisors, delivery teams, and relationship managers, ensuring continuity of client strategy and effective knowledge transfer across engagements.
Represent BDC Advisory Services externally through thought leadership, content development, speaking engagements, and participation in targeted events that promote Business and Organizational Capabilities solutions. At BDC, we think and act differently, and we value inclusion, equity, and authenticity—you can be yourself at work while making a tangible impact on Canadian businesses.
WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR
Required Qualifications (Must‑Have)
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Management, Strategy, or a related discipline.
Minimum
10 years of progressive experience
in a consulting environment, with senior responsibility for:
Enterprise‑level strategic planning
Executive advisory to entrepreneurs and senior management teams
Leading complex, customized consulting mandates
Demonstrated experience advising SMEs or mid‑market organizations.
Proven experience in
business strategy consulting
, including
mergers and acquisitions (M&A)
and
post‑merger integration (PMI)
.
Ability to operate at both strategic and execution levels, translating enterprise strategy into actionable, measurable plans.
Strong engagement and project management capabilities, including oversight of
multiple concurrent mandates or portfolios of work
.
Experience managing risk, quality, governance, and stakeholder expectations across consulting engagements.
Executive‑level communication and presentation skills, with credibility to influence senior stakeholders and support high‑stakes advisory and sales conversations.
Experience supporting consulting business development activities, including diagnostics, proposal development, and client pursuits.
Preferred Qualifications (Nice‑to‑Have)
MBA or equivalent advanced degree or professional designation.
Experience contributing to the development or scaling of consulting methodologies, tools, or Centres of Expertise.
Exposure to
emerging technologies
, including
artificial intelligence
, and their impact on enterprise strategy and organizational transformation.
Experience managing or overseeing a
portfolio of consulting projects delivered by other consultants
.
Experience representing a consulting practice through thought leadership, speaking engagements, or external market visibility initiatives.

Join a team shaping Canada’s venture capital ecosystem
At BDC, the Government Funds team manages capital on behalf of the Government of Canada to strengthen and grow Canada’s venture capital market. This includes deploying
$350M under the Venture Capital Action Plan (VCAP)
,
$450M under the Venture Capital Catalyst Initiative (VCCI)
, and
$450M under the Renewed Venture Capital Catalyst Initiative (Renewed VCCI)
. These programs totalling $1.2B AUM are designed to
crowd in private capital
and support fund managers across the Canadian venture capital asset class.
Building on this foundation, BDC is now deploying the
$1B Growth Venture Capital Catalyst Initiative (Growth VCCI)
, a landmark platform focused on scaling Canada’s most promising funds and innovative companies.
This is a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of
investment, policy, and ecosystem development
, with direct exposure to the most prominent Canadian fund managers while contributing to a
national priority initiative shaping Canada’s innovation economy
.
POSITION OVERVIEW
As Director, you will combine leadership, investment expertise, and complex project management to support the deployment and oversight of government-backed venture capital programs, including VCAP, VCCI, Renewed VCCI, and upcoming Growth VCCI.
You will play a lead role in investment execution, stakeholder management, and portfolio governance, while engaging closely with fund managers, institutional partners, and internal stakeholders including Government.
CHALLENGES TO BE MET
Investment Expertise
Lead complex business and legal negotiations with fund managers and external stakeholders for execution of program delivery including fund investments.
Provide strategic oversight of investment activities across the portfolio, ensuring alignment between policy objectives, portfolio construction considerations, and market dynamics
Provide senior investment judgment and guidance on fund performance, risk management, and portfolio development matters
Fund Oversight & Governance
Serve as BDC’s representative on portfolio funds’ LPACs and other governance bodies
Monitor fund performance, governance, and compliance with fund agreements and program requirements
Provide strategic insight and constructive challenge to support strong governance practices and enhance fund outcomes
Guide fund managers on governance and operational best practices to strengthen the long-term sustainability of the venture capital ecosystem
Leadership and Team Management
Demonstrate leadership in team meetings and operations processes, ensuring effective resource allocation, quality control, operational excellence, and alignment with strategic priorities
Ensure the timely and accurate execution of operational activities, including capital calls, distributions, reporting, and stakeholder deliverables
Provide coaching, mentorship, and leadership to a team of Analysts, fostering a collaborative, high-performance culture focused on continuous improvement and professional development
Identify capability and capacity gaps, oversee recruitment and onboarding activities, and promote knowledge sharing and best practices across the team
Program Delivery & Stakeholder Management
Provide strategic input into the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of current and future government investment programs
Respond to complex and time-sensitive requests from internal and external stakeholders while maintaining a high standard of service and professionalism
Oversee the preparation and dissemination of quarterly and annual reporting, performance dashboards, and stakeholder communications
Ensure high standards of quality, consistency, accuracy, and timeliness across all reporting outputs and program deliverables
Portfolio & Ecosystem Leadership
Build and maintain strong relationships with fund managers, institutional investors, ecosystem stakeholders, and government partners
Represent BDC Capital and Government Funds at industry conferences, panels, events, and stakeholder forums
Stay closely connected to venture capital trends, market developments, and emerging opportunities to support strategic decision-making
Support and lead thought leadership initiatives, market studies, and research projects that generate insights from government investment programs and portfolio activities
WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR
Experience and qualifications
Minimum of a Bachelor degree in Commerce or a related discipline (finance, accounting, law or business administration preferred), or an equivalent combination of academic training and relevant professional experience
10 years+ experience in venture capital, private equity, or growth investing, with direct exposure to deal-making at the fund level as well as investment underwriting, structuring, business and legal negotiations and execution
Demonstrated expertise in venture capital fund structures, LPAs, governance frameworks, and policy-driven investment programs
Demonstrated ability to lead complex negotiations and manage multiple high-priority initiatives simultaneously
Significant experience serving on LPACs, Boards of Directors, or equivalent governance bodies
Ability to manage complex stakeholder relationships involving fund managers, institutional investors, government representatives, and senior executives
Strong understanding of the Canadian venture capital ecosystem and a well-established network of industry relationships
Experience leading, coaching, and developing high-performing teams
Core competencies
Strong strategic and investment judgment
Demonstrated leadership and people management capabilities
Excellent communication, influencing, and stakeholder management skills
Ability to align operational execution with broader policy, program, and organizational objectives
High level of rigour, organization, and attention to detail
Ability to operate effectively in a complex, fast-paced, multi-stakeholder environment
Collaborative mindset with a commitment to team development, knowledge sharing, and excellence
The position is primarily based in Montreal or Ottawa, with a preference for these locations. Toronto is also acceptable.

POSITION OVERVIEW
BDC’s Thrive Venture Fund (TVF) is the largest of its kind globally, investing in Canada’s leading female entrepreneurs to drive transformative impact. The $300M fund was launched in the Fall of 2022 with a focused objective of investing in women-led, high-growth, innovative technology companies in Canada.
Our investments in female entrepreneurs are bringing game changing solutions to some of the world’s biggest challenges across industries and sectors. We seek highly driven founders and teams who are leveraging breakthrough innovations in technology with triple bottom line vision: focusing on people, planet and profit. TVF is sector and stage agnostic and invests in high-growth companies with highly scalable market potential that bring together the best innovation, team, and resources to transform today’s markets.
In this role, you will develop your ability to lead a deal end-to-end. You are expected to understand the big picture and the small details of the investment process and represent BDC Capital professionally before its partners.
As an Associate Principal, you will be an integral member of our investment team and involved in all aspects of the investment and portfolio management process. You will assist the team in building and managing an existing and growing portfolio of investments, work on new investments and help us build the next fund to support even more women in tech in Canada. The next generation of exceptional Canadian technology champions will be led by women and funded by BDC’s Thrive Venture Fund.
CHALLENGES TO BE MET
Platform Building
Assist in managing the deal pipeline, reviewing quarterly/bi-annual reports and value assessments before Partner sign-off, and providing financial analysis
Support other team members as appropriate during the development stage of an investment
Ensure that the investment research files, business plans and other collected information are maintained in conformity with BDC’s policies and procedures
Keep new and existing investment files properly documented by monitoring investments, amendments, and disbursements, including financial analysis and forecasting
Deal Sourcing
Cultivate relationships with entrepreneurs and ecosystem partners, relaying any relevant information upwards
Build and maintain networks within the investment community, acting as an ambassador for the fund, BDC Capital and BDC
Stay on top of the current portfolio, identifying companies that are likely to raise funds and discussing potential new or follow-on investments with Partners
Perform market research and scouting to inform the fund’s investment strategy, identifying emerging markets, verticals, technologies, or companies
Conduct initial business plan reviews, manage initial communications with entrepreneurs and referring sources, prepare initial interview memoranda with recommendations to pursue or decline deals
Deal Making
Coordinate and lead due diligence for new and/or existing investment opportunities by conducting analyses such as market, competition, management, sales, products, cap table, and anything that is relevant to determining potential business value and exit strategies
Determine and validate performance metrics, creating valuation models, forecasts and financial pro formas
Conduct reference calls with competitors, clients, industry experts, and prospect companies’ current or past employees
Follow up on investments using appropriate databases, customer interactions, internet sites, research reports and other investment resources
Validate, audit and fact-check information provided by companies
Develop and maintain appropriate information resources and subject matter expertise in various industries, markets, and business trends
Produce Investment Memos and support Partners in presenting opportunities to the Investment Committee
Portfolio Management & Support
Monitor portfolio performance, comparing performance to forecasts and models, and relaying potential opportunities and issues to management
Take ownership of a select group of companies, monitoring them and providing value-added support, taking charge of operational communication, participating in board meetings as an observer, and keeping abreast of developments to escalate critical issues to Partners
Assist Partners in managing efficient ongoing relationships with executives of investee companies, promptly responding to all inquiries in a courteous and timely manner
Assist portfolio companies with introductions (e.g., potential suppliers, investors, employees), governance, financing, strategic planning, marketing, and other operational topics
WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR
Typical Background
5 to 7 years of experience in a role involving structured thinking, financial analysis, and technical expertise. These profiles are likely to come from, but are not limited to:
Finance roles: venture capital, private equity, investment banking, accounting firms
Operator roles: technology startup, industry-leading corporation, industry specialist
Advisory roles: consulting, law, corporate strategy, corporate development
Bachelor’s degree in Commerce, Economics, Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics (STEM). Other degrees are viable if the professional has strong analytical skills
A post-graduate degree or equivalent certification is valuable. Typical post-graduate credentials are likely to be, but are not limited to:
Master’s degree in business administration (MBA)
Other STEM Master’s or PhD degree
Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA)
Technical Knowledge
Thorough understanding of the deal process, from sourcing to due diligence, to portfolio management
Strong skills in Excel, particularly in building robust financial models that include sensitivity analysis and scenario modeling, as well as performing complex data analysis. Any other analytic tools and techniques are an asset
Excellent ability to problem-solve using structured thinking and communication techniques
Excellent ability to use other MS suite applications efficiently, mainly Word and PowerPoint
Ability to write an Investment Memo that is clear, concise, and compelling
Proficiency with using AI tools
Technology skills with wide application, such as coding, chemistry, or electronics, can be an asset
Operational knowledge of any technical industry is an asset
Bilingualism in French and English is an asset

Credit Investments invests globally across leveraged finance, real estate and infrastructure lending, structured credit and special situations. The Role
The Total Fund Management (“TFM”) department is responsible for the successful implementation of the Fund’s investment framework. These activities are focused primarily on the Strategic Portfolio, our long term vision for the intended investment portfolio composition five or more years into the future. TFM also works on the Total Fund daily investment cycle, including all the processes, systems, and data needed to structure the investment portfolio in response to the ongoing flow of cash and exposures into and out of the Fund. TFM consists of five groups: Portfolio Design, Research & Engineering; Beta, Collateral & Liquidity Management; Dynamic Portfolio Management; Trading; and Strategy & Business Management.
The Portfolio Design, Research & and Engineering (“PDRE”) group defines the strategic portfolios which enshrine key decisions including exposure, leverage, liquidity, currency targets and size of the Active Portfolio. The group develops and maintains the research, methodologies, quantitative models, analytical tools, and engineering capabilities that support strategic allocation, portfolio management, tactical asset allocation, implementation research, trading and the Office of the CIO where applicable.
We are recruiting for a 12-month contract at the Portfolio Manager level for our Total Portfolio Design & Targets (TPDT) team within PDRE. The Portfolio Manager will work closely with teams across TFM to design, evaluate, and implement robust frameworks for Total Fund exposure management. While activities are underpinned by systematic, model-driven approaches, the role also involves the application of investment judgement in the management of exposures, including the assessment and execution of adjustments and overrides where appropriate. The role will also contribute to efforts to assess complementarities across strategic and tactical horizons.

Accountabilities
Contribute to providing recommendations to the senior management team on total portfolio targets and asset allocation.
Maintain and enhance existing models used for portfolio construction and analysis.
Perform ad-hoc quantitative analysis and effectively communicate findings and recommendations
Apply programming expertise, optimization, linear algebra or numerical analysis techniques to prototype portfolio analytics and quantitative models used in top-down portfolio management. Convey new information requirements through written specifications.
Mentor and develop experienced team members by providing guidance on advanced technical problem-solving, portfolio construction, and investment decision-making.
Qualifications
At least 7-10 years of relevant experience in portfolio management and/or asset allocation research. Expertise across multiple asset classes, including equity, fixed income and currency, and a strong understanding of macro drivers of returns and cross-asset linkages are considered assets.
Experience applying empirical statistical and quantitative techniques to financial and macroeconomic data. Experience with AI-assisted coding tools and the ability to leverage them effectively to enhance modeling and portfolio analysis are assets.
Strong programming and quantitative skills; demonstrable proficiency using Python.
Ability to quickly grasp new concepts and work in a high-performing culture, under pressure and with time-sensitive deadlines.
Graduate degree in Finance, Economics, Mathematics, Engineering, or a related discipline preferred.
Effective communication skills across a broad range of stakeholders.
Self‑motivated, organized, flexible, and adaptable to changing priorities and new challenges.

A place with purpose. CBC/Radio-Canada has always been a highly regarded pioneer of media technology — not just in Canada but around the world. Your Role
The Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) AI Lab at CBC/Radio-Canada operates as an agile, high-performance innovation hub. Our mission is to prototype, experiment with and deploy artificial intelligence solutions for media production systems across the organization. We design customized functionalities and seamlessly integrate advanced AI technologies into our existing product ecosystem.
We are looking for an AI Analyst who is pragmatic, curious, ambitious and ready to kick-start their career in applied AI. Backed by senior experts, you will work in a highly experimental environment where your initiatives will have real, immediate impact.
Our team is supported on a day-to-day basis by next-generation coding assistants like Cursor and Claude to optimize ideation, development, debugging and documentation. Play an active role in the full life cycle (prototyping, development, deployment) of AI-driven applications and features, with a specific focus on cloud architectures.
Help fine-tune, evaluate and integrate large language models (LLMs) into our core business processes.
Set up and maintain testing, monitoring, feedback and performance assessment protocols for our AI systems.
Assist the team in connecting intelligent agents to internal or external services and APIs (using the MCP protocol or equivalent tool frameworks).
Work closely with cross-functional teams (product, architecture, data science) to embed AI capabilities into our digital platforms.
Conduct exploratory proofs of concept to bridge AI with our legacy systems and build viable new products.
Leverage AI co-pilots to accelerate your development workflow while maintaining strict standards for test coverage, code quality and IT security.

University degree in software engineering, computer science, data science or a related field.
One to two years’ hands-on technical experience in software design (gained through internships, academic projects, personal initiatives or early professional work).
Strong proficiency in Python, TypeScript or Java, together with an outstanding capacity for continuous learning.
A solid understanding of software engineering fundamentals, including quality control, debugging, testing methodologies and information security.

Professional or personal projects involving machine learning, LLMs, RAG architectures or autonomous agent development.
Keen interest in the media industry, audiovisual production, entertainment or creative technologies.
Familiarity with cloud ecosystems and modern AI libraries or frameworks (PyTorch, CrewAI, LangGraph, etc.).
Demonstrated practical experience with AI-assisted coding tools like Claude and Cursor.
Active involvement in the open-source community or a portfolio of exploratory AI projects.

About CBC News Podcasts
Canada’s best journalism, on demand and delivered directly into your earholes.
Our mandate is to amplify our news journalism in the podcast space, and that means video and social media are key to our podcasting strategy.
We work with CBC teams in several ways;
producing original always-on news podcasts like Front Burner and Two Blocks from the White House

assisting network audio and video teams to increase their podcasting presence
developing original news podcast series like See You In Court and upcoming investigative series.

The successful candidate for this position will be a creative thinker who puts audience needs at the centre of their decision-making, ensuring our podcast video content performs across all platforms, including CBC’s owned and operated apps, YouTube and TikTok.
You are at the leading edge of changing audience consumption trends in the digital space. You have a deep understanding of the values of public broadcasting, and the importance of news journalism.
You are a natural visual storyteller, and have both the editorial and technical skills needed to keep up in a deadline-driven production environment. You use data to make decisions and stay on top of consumption patterns.

Determines the order and importance of various elements of a program.

Identifies, develops, and maintains contacts appropriate to the area of assignment.

Oversees the shooting, editing, encoding, digitizing, and packaging of digital audio and video for the internet.
Prepares programs for the internet, including coding, and manipulating images and graphics.

.

University degree or equivalent and ten years' experience, of which five must involve work in broadcasting or a closely related industry.
Significant experience producing live international multi-sports event programming.
Experience writing, editing, and conceptualizing the content and flow of distinctive programming.
Desirable experience in sports journalism; must demonstrate solid editorial knowledge of national and international sports news and issues.
Extensive knowledge of international professional and amateur sports (with special emphasis on Olympic sports).
Proven ability and experience working with a sales/revenue department developing programming to meet client needs, programming objectives, and financial goals.
Experience meeting and presenting programming concepts to clients, sponsors, and agencies.
Strong leadership skills to motivate a programming team, on-air talent, and hosts.
Ability to forward-plan while remaining topical and current.
Highly developed interpersonal skills, able to communicate effectively and cooperatively (established relationships with Canadian Sports Federations are an asset).
A proven understanding of the CBC and the relationship between Sports, the network, and regional programming.

ABOUT THE ROLE
Are you deeply curious about how the media and advertising ecosystem really works under the hood? We are seeking a high-caliber early-career analyst (fresh graduate in Business Management, Technology, or Futuresight-related disciplines) who possesses relentless intellectual curiosity and an appetite to explore the complex intersections that others overlook.
In this role, you will analyze the media ecosystem end-to-end—spanning commercial advertising models, digital distribution mechanics, subscription economics, and emerging tech stacks. You will be expected to thrive in uncertainty, challenge assumptions, and produce rigorous, evidence-backed insights to guide executive decision-making.
KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES & RESPONSIBILITIES
Ecosystem & Vendor Intelligence:
Deliver comprehensive vendor dossiers and category analyses within tight timelines, evaluating category fit, integration feasibility, exit costs, vendor viability, and clear decision confidence levels.
End-to-End Media Economics Research:
Map and analyze the overlapping dependencies between commercial ad mechanics, audience measurement, first-party data strategies, social tech platforms, and subscription revenue streams.
Rigorous Pilot & Hypothesis Testing:
Pre-register every pilot with clear hypotheses, success metrics, stop conditions, and market-as-control measurement designs before execution. Ensure all test results produce actionable, decision-grade findings rather than anecdotal summaries.
Governance & Constraint Screening:
Rigorously screen all technical and strategic recommendations against procurement, legal, privacy, and regulatory boundaries before presenting to leadership forums.
Competitive & Supply Chain Tracking:
Monitor industry shifts including programmatic supply chain developments, unified sales platforms, broadcaster consolidation, and platform-side API/policy changes.
Quantified Impact:
Track, validate, and own the quantification of vendor spend avoided and value unlocked through strategic analysis.
SKILLS & QUALIFICATIONS SOUGHT
Education:
Bachelor's degree in Business Management, Business Analytics, Technology Information Systems, Innovation Strategy, or a related field (Recent Graduates encouraged).
Structured Research & Synthesis:
Exceptional writing and analytical skills with a disciplined focus on writing for executive decision-making rather than word count.
Exceptional Technical Documentation:
Expertise in translating complex technical parameters and multi-dimensional tech transformations into clear, visual, and highly structured business summaries (such as matrices and process maps).
Skeptical & Evidence-Driven Mindset:
Skeptical by disposition; naturally treats vendor claims and market hype as unproven hypotheses requiring rigorous empirical proof.
Comfort with Uncertainty & Tech Stacks:
Eager to navigate complex, multi-layered environments involving programmatic infrastructure, log-level ad data, SSP/ad server reporting, and data clean rooms.
Financial & Statistical Literacy:
Capability to build financial models sufficient to size revenue opportunities and integration costs, and statistical literacy to distinguish actual signal from noise.
Uncompromising Integrity:
Willingness to state uncertainty explicitly and report negative or failing pilot results clearly without softening outcomes.
WHY JOIN US?
This position offers a rare launchpad for a forward-thinking graduate to work at the intersection of business strategy, commercial tech, and future market dynamics. You will have direct exposure to executive decision-makers (including C-level leadership) and the autonomy to investigate complex industry challenges end-to-end.

title: Associate Portfolio Manager, Public Credit
description:
At IMCO, our talent is among the best! IMCO offers a uniquely stimulating and rewarding environment where you can help build and drive organizational transformation, all while seeking to challenge yourself, learn, and grow your career.
Our culture is built on collaboration and passion, with a shared commitment to delivering lasting value to the clients we serve. Located in downtown Toronto, our vision is to be the partner of choice for Ontario’s public sector funds and to build a high-performing, value-driven asset management firm.
This job posting is for an existing vacancy. If you are ready to deliver best-in-class service and join a collaborative, motivated and fun team of professionals, IMCO offers the opportunity to do impactful work and broaden your expertise.
If you’re looking to use your expertise to drive strategic outcomes, we’d love to hear from you.
‎
IMCO’s actively managed Global Credit strategy (~$10.1B AUM) delivers higher risk-adjusted returns through a unified approach to credit investing, integrating public and private credit within a single, globally diversified portfolio. The strategy adopts a holistic approach to portfolio construction, allocating across public credit segments, including investment grade, high yield, leveraged loans, and structured credit, alongside private credit segments to capture relative value opportunities, enhance diversification, and optimize liquidity and return outcomes across market cycles.
Our collaborative culture and value-add approach to strategic partnerships makes us a preferred partner to some of the largest investors in the world. We have a targeted strategy to grow our highly diversified Global Credit portfolio and are looking for a highly motivated Associate Portfolio Manager to join our Global Credit team with a focus on public credit!
The Associate Portfolio Manager, Public Credit will play a key role in managing IMCO’s externally managed Public Credit portfolio, with responsibilities spanning manager selection and due diligence, portfolio strategy and construction, and ongoing monitoring and oversight. The role combines rigorous investment analysis with active portfolio management, while also contributing to ongoing initiatives to enhance the Global Credit platform and target operating model, including the implementation of investment systems and processes and the development of advanced analytics and AI capabilities to improve portfolio insights and support investment decision-making.
As a Member of Our Global Credit Team, You Will Contribute Across Three Core Areas: Manager Selection & Oversight, Portfolio Management and Strategy, and Platform Enhancement:
Provide analytical and portfolio management support to the Managing Director in overseeing externally managed public credit portfolios on a day-to-day basis, including ad hoc analysis and strategic initiatives.
Source, screen, and conduct due diligence on external public credit managers across strategies (e.g., investment grade, high yield, loans and structured credit), utilizing data platforms and AI-enabled tools to analyze performance, identify risks, and support manager screening and ongoing evaluation.
Lead and support the preparation of investment recommendations, including drafting investment memos and presentations for internal Investment Committee approval.
Assist in structuring and negotiating investment mandates, guidelines, and negotiating fee arrangements with external managers in collaboration with risk, legal and other internal teams.
Conduct ongoing monitoring of external managers, including performance attribution, risk exposures, style drift, and adherence to investment guidelines; leverage AI to enhance efficiency in analysis, identify performance and risk trends, and support the development of portfolio-level reporting and insights for senior management.
Lead or contribute to initiatives within Global Credit to enhance portfolio management infrastructure through the application of AI and the integration of new investment systems and analytics capabilities; partner with internal teams (Risk, Performance, Operations, Technology) to improve investment data quality to enable more effective analysis, reporting, and decision-making.
Support portfolio construction and strategic asset allocation across public credit, including contributing to capital allocation decisions across segments and managers, and shaping overall portfolio strategy.
Maintain a strong understanding of global public credit markets, including macroeconomic trends, interest rates, credit spreads, and technical factors, to inform manager selection and portfolio positioning.
Engage regularly with external managers through diligence meetings, portfolio reviews, and on-site visits to assess portfolio strategy, market outlook, and execution capabilities.
Support client and stakeholder reporting, including preparation of quarterly updates, market commentary, and materials for senior management and board-level discussions.
What do you need to succeed?
Minimum 5+ years of experience in asset management, with a focus on public credit investing and manager selection and oversight.
Experience leveraging data analytics and AI-enabled tools to support investment research, manager evaluation, or portfolio insights.
Strong understanding of global public credit markets, including corporate bonds, leveraged loans, structured credit, and credit market dynamics.
Experience conducting due diligence on external investment managers, including evaluation of investment processes, portfolio construction, and risk management.
Experience in private debt / private credit or broader private markets is considered an asset.
Undergraduate degree required. CFA designation, MBA or master’s degree(s) are considered an asset.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to synthesize complex investment information into clear, actionable insights.
Effective communicator with the ability to present investment recommendations and market views to senior stakeholders.
Collaborative team player with an appreciation for diverse perspectives and a high-performing team environment.
Self-starter who can engage and motivate other people around key ideas, effectively listen and provide constructive feedback to others, participate in discussion and brainstorming.
Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to build and maintain relationships with internal teams and external managers.

title: Tissue Coordinator
description:
À Santé Ontario, nous sommes résolus à bâtir une solide culture organisationnelle qui unifie et responsabilise tous les membres de notre équipe à travers la province. Notre vision est qu'ensemble, nous serons des responsables en matière de santé et de bien-être pour tous. Notre mission est d'interconnecter le système de santé afin de favoriser l'amélioration et l'équité des résultats, des expériences et de la valeur en matière de santé. Notre façon de travailler ensemble se reflète dans nos cinq valeurs, l'intégrité, l'inspiration, la ténacité, l'humilité et l'attention.
Envie de donner un nouveau souffle à votre carrière?  Saisissez cette opportunité!
Rattaché à :
Responsable, PRC - Tissu
Classification :
Coordonnateur des tissus
Lieu de travail :
483, rue Bay, Toronto
Calendrier :
Combinaison de quarts de travail de 12 heures en semaine et le week-end
Type d'emploi
:
à temps partiel permanent
(0.75 ETP)
Taux horaire :
de 34,13 $ à 42,65 $
Le Réseau Trillium pour le don de vie (TGLN), qui fait partie de Santé Ontario, est responsable de la coordination du don et de la transplantation d’organes et de tissus en Ontario. Notre mandat comprend la sensibilisation accrue du public à l’importance du don d’organes et de tissus, la formation des professionnels de la santé et la mise en place d’un système de don et de transplantation sûr et efficace en Ontario. En travaillant en collaboration avec nos parties prenantes et en favorisant la croissance organisationnelle et individuelle, nous valorisons l'honnêteté, la confiance, le respect et la compassion.
Nous recherchons actuellement un coordinateur de tissus
à temps partiel permanent
(0,75 ETP) très motivé (TC). Le titulaire du poste devra fournir des services professionnels liés au don de tissus d'une manière conforme à la mission et aux valeurs de TGLN. Le coordinateur des tissus finalise les procédures de sélection des donneurs, contacte les familles pour obtenir leur consentement au don, s'assure de l'acceptation des tissus par différentes banques de tissus, coordonne les activités de prélèvement et effectue un suivi auprès des familles après le don pour les tissus non prélevés ayant fait l'objet d'un consentement
Voici ce que vous allez faire :
Activités de sélection des donneurs : Évaluation de l'aptitude clinique du donneur et recueil des antécédents médicaux et sociaux en concertation avec la famille
Approche de consentement téléphonique : Contacter les familles par téléphone pour les informer du processus de don et obtenir leur consentement au don
Coordination des cas : mise à disposition de différents tissus à différentes banques en fournissant les antécédents médicaux et sociaux nécessaires du donneur, le transfert du corps, la négociation de la date et du lieu de l’intervention chirurgicale, et les services hospitaliers.
Soutien aux familles de donneurs
Chef d'équipe (lorsqu'il est désigné)
Assurance qualité
Loi sur la santé et la sécurité au travail et l’accessibilité pour les personnes handicapées de l’Ontario
Répond aux appels des hôpitaux référents reçus au Centre provincial de ressources, effectue une évaluation préliminaire des antécédents du patient et identifie toutes les options de don pertinentes;
Fournit des services de consultation en tant qu'expert en matière de don de tissus;
Évalue la consultation d'experts concernant la pertinence des tissus ou d'autres problèmes médicaux, le cas échéant
Fournit aux banques de tissus des informations complètes concernant l'adéquation des donneurs et des tissus en vue de leur prélèvement. Les informations sont fournies conformément à la législation en vigueur sur la protection de la vie privée et aux politiques de confidentialité de TGLN
Réalisation en temps opportun du bilan médico-social, généralement au moment du don, parfois à une date et une heure convenues à l'avance afin de minimiser les occasions manquées.
Il contacte le décideur suppléant en temps opportun et le recontacte si nécessaire pour obtenir son consentement au don de tissus
Apprend et applique de nouvelles techniques et stratégies d'approche
Participe à la formation continue et à la sensibilisation à l'évaluation
Assure la liaison en permanence avec le personnel sur place (c.-à-d. OTDC, professionnels de la santé et personnel de rétablissement) de l'hôpital référent pour effectuer l'évaluation des risques, le dépistage, les tests et l'évaluation de l'adéquation des tissus individuels après consentement;
Collabore avec le bureau du coroner pour faciliter le don de tissus et transmet les cas au coroner superviseur régional au cas par cas;
Obtient des privilèges chirurgicaux temporaires pour le personnel de prélèvement de tissus, lorsque cela est nécessaire, conformément aux politiques de l'hôpital référent, en veillant à ce que le processus d'accréditation soit en place au moment opportun;
Coordonne le calendrier et la confirmation de la disponibilité de la salle de réveil (OR) et de l'arrivée des équipes de prélèvement de tissus;
Transmet toutes les informations pertinentes concernant le donneur au personnel compétent en matière de prélèvement de tissus et à la banque de tissus concernée;
S'assure que le ou les services hospitaliers concernés soient contactés après le prélèvement des tissus afin d'assurer le transport rapide du corps vers la maison funéraire.
Communique et interagit avec les membres de la famille;
Informe les familles lorsque les possibilités de don ne peuvent être menées à terme malgré un consentement signé
Assume la responsabilité du travail du groupe pendant un quart de travail donné;
Priorise et attribue le travail, y compris les cas actifs de don de tissus, le suivi et la clôture des cas de référence précoce, les tâches de suivi;
Supervise l'attribution du tutorat aux nouveaux employés afin de garantir que le nouveau membre de l'équipe ait la possibilité d'apprendre et d'atteindre les objectifs d'orientation;
Diffuse un rapport de quart précis;
Assure le suivi et l'attribution des dossiers et de leur clôture avec l'équipe PRC-Tissue;
Suivi des dossiers de dons d'organes en cours et de leur statut en vue d'un don de tissus
Utilise son expérience et son jugement cliniques pour répondre aux questions relatives à la compatibilité tissulaire avant de faire intervenir le médecin responsable ou le médecin consultant;
S'assure que, lorsqu'ils ne sont pas désignés comme chef d'équipe, les TC de service sont responsables de suivre les directives du chef d'équipe.
Assure la responsabilité de la saisie en temps voulu et de l'exactitude des données dans tous les systèmes électroniques et les dossiers papier;
Assume la responsabilité de documenter et de signaler les écarts par rapport aux IPC et les plaintes;
Assume la responsabilité du respect des politiques et procédures/CPI (cliniques et administratives).
Voici ce dont vous aurez besoin pour réussir :
Formation et expérience
Un diplôme universitaire ou collégial en sciences de la santé, en sciences biologiques ou dans une discipline équivalente reconnue est requis
Une certification en banque d'yeux ou de tissus (technicien certifié en banque d'yeux (CEBT)/spécialiste certifié en banque de tissus (CTBS)), en banque de sang, en tant qu'infirmier(ère) auxiliaire autorisé(e) (IAA) ou ambulancier(ère) paramédical(e) est un atout.
Une expérience professionnelle d'au moins trois (3) ans dans le domaine du don d'organes et de tissus, des sciences de la santé ou des soins de santé, ainsi que dans la récupération et le traitement des tissus, est préférable
Une expérience dans un établissement de soins de santé ou auprès de patients et de leurs familles en période de crise est préférable
Capacité à travailler par quarts de 12 heures dans un environnement fonctionnant 24h/24 et 7j/7, incluant les jours, les nuits et les heures creuses.  De plus, il est obligatoire de travailler les week-ends et les jours fériés.
Tous les horaires de jour exigent une présence au bureau
Connaissances et compétences
Une connaissance approfondie des sciences biologiques et de la santé ainsi que des normes d'assurance qualité est un atout
Capacité à maintenir et à protéger la confidentialité des patients en tout temps, en faisant preuve de discrétion et de discernement
Aptitudes démontrées en gestion du temps, avec la capacité et la flexibilité nécessaires pour prioriser plusieurs tâches et projets dans un environnement dynamique et axé sur les résultats
Personne motivée et autonome, capable de travailler aussi bien seule qu'en équipe
Excellentes aptitudes à la communication écrite et orale
Précision et souci du détail
Solides compétences informatiques
Lieu de travail :
Toronto, On

Un membre de l’équipe communiquera avec vous dans les 48 heures.
Tissue Coordinator
At Ontario Health, we are committed to developing a strong organizational culture that connects and inspires all team members across the province. Our vision is that together, we will be a leader in health and wellness for all. Our mission is to connect the health system to drive improved and equitable health outcomes, experiences and value. How we work together is reflected through our five values: integrity, inspiration, tenacity, humility and care
Want to make a difference in your career?  Consider this opportunity!
Reporting to:
Manager, PRC - Tissue
Classification:
Tissue Coordinator
Worksite:
483 Bay Street, Toronto
Schedule:
Combination of weekday and weekend 12 hour shifts
Employment Type
:  Permanent Part time (0.75 fte)
Rate of Pay:
$34.13 to $42.65 per hour
Trillium Gift of Life Network (TGLN), part of Ontario Health, is responsible for the coordination of organ and tissue donation and transplantation in Ontario. Our mandate includes increasing public awareness of the importance of organ and tissue donation, education of health care professionals, and ensuring a safe and effective donation and transplant system in Ontario. Working collaboratively with our stakeholders and fostering organizational and individual growth, we value honesty, trust, respect and compassion.
We are currently seeking a highly motivated permanent part time (0.75)  Tissue Coordinator (TC). The incumbent shall provide professional services related to tissue donation in a manner consistent with the mission and values of TGLN. The Tissue Coordinator completes processes for donor screening, approaches families for consent to donate, secures acceptance of tissues by various tissue banks, coordinates recovery activities, and conducts family follow up post-donation for consented non-recovered tissues
Here is what you will be doing:
Donor Screening Activities: Assessment of clinical suitability of donor and completion of medical/social history in consultation with family
Telephone Consent Approach: Engaging in telephone approach to families regarding the donation process and securing consent to donate from family members
Case Coordination: offering various tissues to various banks by providing necessary donor medical/social history, body transfer, negotiating OR time and location, and hospital services.
Donor Family Support
Team Lead (when assigned)
Quality assurance
Occupational Health and Safety/ Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act
Responds to calls from referring hospitals received in the Provincial Resource Centre, conducts a preliminary assessment of the patient’s history and identifies all relevant donation options;
Provides consultation services as an expert in matters relating to tissue donation;
Assesses expert consultation regarding tissue suitability or other medical issues as appropriate
Provides complete information to the tissue bank(s) concerning donor and tissue suitability for placement of tissues. The information is provided in a manner that complies with existing privacy legislation and TGLN confidentiality policies
Timely completion of the med-soc, usually at time of donation, occasionally at a pre-arranged date and time to minimize missed opportunities.
Approaches the substitute decision maker in a timely manner, and re-approaches when necessary to obtain consent for tissue donation
Learns and applies new techniques and strategies for approach
Participates in ongoing education and evaluation awareness
Liaises continuously with on-site personnel (ie. OTDC, health-care professionals and recovery staff) at referring hospital to complete risk assessment, screening, testing and evaluation of individual tissue suitability after consent;
Works with the coroner’s office to facilitate tissue donation and escalates cases to Regional Supervising Coroner on a case by case basis;
Obtains temporary surgical privileges for tissue recovery personnel, when necessary, in accordance with the policies of the referring hospital, ensuring compliance with the credentialing process is in place at the time;
Coordinates timing and confirmation of recovery facility (OR) availability and arrival of tissue recovery teams;
Conveys all relevant information regarding the donor to the appropriate tissue recovery personnel and relevant Tissue Bank;
Ensures relevant hospital department(s) are contacted following tissue recovery for timely transport of body to funeral home.
Communicates and engages with family members;
Informs families when donation opportunities cannot go forward despite a signed consent
Takes accountability for the work of the group during a given shift;
Prioritizes and assigns work including active tissue donation cases, early referral case follow up and closure, follow up tasks;
Oversees the assignment of preceptorship of new employees to ensure new team member is given the opportunity to learn and meet orientation objectives;
Distributes an accurate shift report;
Monitors and assigns case follow up and case closure with PRC-Tissue Team;
Tracks active organ cases and their status for tissue offering
Uses clinical experience and judgment to answer TC questions prior to involving the MOC or involving the consulting physician regarding tissue suitability;
Ensures, when not assigned Team Lead, TCs on shift are responsible for following the Team Lead’s direction.
Takes responsibility for timeliness and accuracy of data entered into all electronic systems and paper charting;
Takes responsibility for documenting and reporting variance(s) from CPI’s and complaint(s);
Takes responsibility for compliance with policies and procedures/CPIs (both Clinical and Administrative).
Here is what you will need to be successful:
Education and Experience
University degree or college diploma in health sciences, biological sciences or a recognized equivalent major is required
Certification in eye or tissue banking (Certified Eye Bank Technician (CEBT)/Certified Tissue Banking Specialist (CTBS), blood banking, as a Registered Practical Nurse (RPN) or a paramedic is an asset
Minimum of three (3) years working experience in organ and tissue donation, health sciences or health care environment, tissue recovery and processing is preferred
Experience in a healthcare setting or working with patients and their families at times of crisis is preferred
Ability to work 12 hour shifts in a 24/7 environment which includes days, nights and mid day.  In addition, there is a requirement to work weekends and statutory holidays.
All days shifts are required to work in office at 483 Bay Street
Knowledge and Skills
In-depth knowledge of biological and health sciences as well as quality assurance standards is an asset
Ability to maintain and protect patient confidentiality at all times, demonstrating use of discretion and sound judgment
Demonstrated time management skills with the ability and flexibility to prioritize multiple tasks and projects in a fast paced, results oriented environment
Motivated self-starter with the ability to work independently and collaboratively as part of a team
Demonstrated superior written and oral communication skills
Accuracy and close attention to detail
Strong computer skills

Toronto, Ontario

groups; 2SLGBTQIA+ communities; trans and nonbinary individuals;

The Health Innovation Pathway (HIP) brings promising innovations into the health system, improving patient outcomes, driving economic growth and helping Ontario’s health system reach its full potential. The Ontario Securities Commission (OSC) is the statutory body responsible for regulating Ontario’s capital markets in accordance with the mandate established in the provincial Securities Act and the Commodity Futures Act. The mandate of the OSC is to provide protection to investors from unfair, improper or fraudulent practices, to foster fair, efficient and competitive capital markets and confidence in the capital markets, to foster capital formation, and to contribute to the stability of the financial system and the reduction of systemic risk. This mandate is performed through policy, operational, and enforcement activities. The OSC also contributes to national and global securities regulation development.
We offer a diverse, fair, and flexible work environment and take pride in our challenging and rewarding work.
The opportunity
Reporting to the Manager, Analytics & Technology Innovation, you will provide strategic leadership and hands-on technical expertise in advanced analytics and data science. You will develop cloud-based analytics products, help shape the OSC’s analytics roadmap, and guide technical staff while collaborating with stakeholders across the organization.
This is an opportunity for an experienced data science professional who combines deep technical capability with strong business judgment, clear communication, and an understanding of capital markets or regulatory environments.
What you will do
Lead the design and delivery of advanced analytics and data science solutions for divisions across the OSC.
Mine, clean, analyze and synthesize large structured and unstructured data sets into useful data products and insights.
Architect, prototype, test and deliver complex cloud-based analytics solutions that demonstrate business value quickly.
Lead multiple analytics projects in parallel, managing deliverables, timelines, service commitments and stakeholder expectations.
Collaborate with stakeholders to clarify needs, onboard and refine data, and translate abstract concepts into tangible deliverables.
Apply Python, artificial intelligence, natural language processing and text mining to solve complex business problems.
Contribute to analytics standards, methodologies, controls and best practices, including code review, quality assurance and knowledge sharing.
Guide and mentor data science team staff, coordinate task-level work, monitor progress and support capability development.
Build training materials and educate OSC staff on new analytics processes and products.
Participate in Agile ceremonies, including sprint planning, backlog refinement, stakeholder demonstrations and daily scrums.
What you bring
Bachelor's degree in mathematics, computer science, computer engineering, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience. A master's degree is considered an asset.
At least five years of relevant experience in data science, advanced analytics or application development.
Experience working in capital markets, a regulatory environment or a financial setting.
Advanced proficiency with Python and experience with analytics or development technologies such as R, Scala, PySpark, Angular or React JS.
Strong experience delivering complex data science solutions using open-source tools and Microsoft Azure services.
Expertise in natural language processing, text mining, artificial intelligence, and structured and unstructured big data.
The ability to assess emerging AI developments and identify practical applications for the organization.
Excellent critical thinking, analytical, decision-making and problem-solving skills.
The ability to communicate complex technical and business concepts clearly to diverse audiences at all levels.
Strong stakeholder relationship, negotiation, organization and prioritization skills, with a results-oriented approach.
Experience mentoring junior staff and helping build stronger technical teams.

operates in a fast-paced, results-oriented environment, conducting initial inquiries into potential breaches of securities law and identifying opportunities to proactively disrupt misconduct before significant investor harm occurs. The team assesses complaints, tips, whistleblower submissions, referrals, and other information received from the public, market participants, regulators, and law enforcement agencies. Through evidence gathering, legal analysis, intelligence development, and collaboration, the team evaluates the nature and extent of potential misconduct and determines the most appropriate regulatory response, including disruption, referral, investigation, resolution, or closure.
The Opportunity
Case Assessment & Disruption is recruiting a Team Lead to oversee complex assessments, intake operations, and proactive disruption activities involving potential securities misconduct and emerging enforcement risks.
Reporting to the Head of Case Assessment & Disruption and supporting the Manager, the Team Lead provides leadership, strategic direction, and operational oversight for the intake and assessment functions. The role ensures matters are effectively triaged, prioritized, and advanced, while supporting the work of a multidisciplinary team responsible for assessing allegations, evaluating evidence, identifying potential breaches of securities law, and recommending appropriate regulatory responses.
The Team Lead also leads proactive disruption initiatives aimed at reducing investor harm and protecting market integrity. This includes identifying emerging risks, developing and implementing strategies to deter misconduct and disrupt harmful activities, and monitoring and reporting on disruption outcomes and trends to support informed decision-making and continuous improvement.
As a senior member of the team, the Team Lead plays a key role in ensuring the Division effectively identifies, prioritizes, and minimizes risk, leverages disruption opportunities, and delivers timely, impactful outcomes in support of the OSC's mandate.
Lead Complex Assessments, Disruption Strategies, and Enforcement Responses
Lead the assessment of complex securities misconduct matters, including fraud, market abuse, misleading disclosure, crypto-related misconduct, and other emerging risks.
Direct assessment strategies, evaluate evidence, identify potential breaches of securities law, and determine appropriate regulatory and enforcement responses of assessment team members.
Identify and oversee disruption opportunities to prevent investor harm, address unlawful activity, and protect market integrity.
Make critical decisions regarding file prioritization, referrals, investigation steps, disruptions, and closures, while promoting the effective use of data analytics, artificial intelligence, and emerging technologies to enhance assessment outcomes and operational effectiveness.
Provide Expert Regulatory Leadership and Operational Oversight
Serve as a subject matter expert in securities law, investigations, evidentiary standards, and enforcement practices, providing strategic advice to the team on complex matters.
Lead, mentor, and develop a multidisciplinary team while fostering a culture of excellence, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
Oversee matters from intake through assessment, ensuring file work is timely, risk-based, and compliant with legislative, policy, and procedural requirements.
Monitor team performance, capacity, outcomes, and operational risks, and report on results, emerging trends, and key performance metrics to support informed decision-making and continuous improvement.
Lead Strategic Partnerships and Continuous Improvement
Build and maintain relationships with regulators, law enforcement, government agencies, and other stakeholders to support enforcement and disruption objectives.
Lead information-sharing, deconfliction, and multi-agency initiatives involving regulatory, criminal, intelligence, and public-interest considerations.
Identify emerging risks, enforcement trends, and market developments and provide strategic advice to senior leadership.
Champion initiatives that enhance assessment effectiveness, disruption capabilities, operational efficiency, and enforcement outcomes.
What's In It For You?
Make a meaningful impact on investors and participants in Ontario's capital markets by helping identify misconduct and prevent investor harm.
Lead a highly specialized team responsible for some of the OSC's most complex, high-risk, and high-profile assessment and disruption matters.
Be at the forefront of innovative regulatory approaches that combine traditional investigative techniques, disruption strategies, data analytics, and collaboration.
Work in a collaborative, progressive, and professionally diverse environment alongside lawyers, investigators, forensic accountants, and specialists.
Influence regulatory outcomes and contribute directly to investor protection, market integrity, and public confidence in Ontario's capital markets.
What Do You Need To Be Successful In This Role?
Required Qualifications
Law Degree (LL.B. or J.D.) and membership in good standing with the Law Society of Ontario, or a CPA designation in good standing.
Minimum 10 years of progressive investigatory experience
in securities enforcement, regulatory investigations, financial crime investigations, regulatory compliance, or a comparable senior investigative role.
Demonstrated leadership experience leading, mentoring, coaching, and developing investigative or regulatory professionals.
Knowledge and Experience
Strong understanding of Ontario securities law, regulatory enforcement processes, and administrative proceedings.
Extensive knowledge of capital markets, investment products, registrants, market participants, and securities regulation.
Significant experience assessing complex allegations of misconduct and making evidence-based regulatory decisions.
Strong understanding of investigative methodologies, evidence collection practices, intelligence development, open-source intelligence techniques, eDiscovery processes, and data analytics.
Experience working with law enforcement agencies, regulators, self-regulatory organizations, government partners, and other stakeholders.
Experience handling complex, sensitive, and high-profile matters involving significant regulatory, legal, reputational, and operational risks.
Experience leading disruption initiatives, intelligence-sharing activities, and coordinated regulatory responses is considered a strong asset.
Leadership Competencies
Proven leadership, mentoring, and coaching abilities.
Strong project management experience overseeing multiple complex files, initiatives, or competing priorities.
Exceptional analytical thinking, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
Ability to think critically, strategically, and creatively in a fast-paced and evolving environment.
Excellent judgment and ability to make sound decisions under pressure.
Outstanding written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex issues clearly and persuasively to staff, executives, regulators, and external stakeholders.
Strong interpersonal and stakeholder management skills with a demonstrated ability to build credibility and influence outcomes.
A collaborative leadership style and commitment to service excellence, accountability, and continuous improvement.

The
Senior Accounting Advisor
will provide expert advice and direction to the Chief Accountant and Associate Chief Accountant, the Commission, and staff on financial reporting and assurance. The role will also involve liaising directly with prominent external stakeholders, including representatives from other provincial and international securities regulators, accounting and assurance standard setters, and the Canadian Public Accountability Board (CPAB).
What you will do
Relying on your strong technical expertise and ability to work collaboratively and build consensus with others, you will:
•    Analyze and resolve complex or novel financial reporting and assurance issues arising in the context of reviews of financial statements and other documents filed under the Ontario Securities Act.
•    Provide advisory services to staff from internal divisions and departments on accounting and assurance matters, which may involve interacting with issuers, their auditors and advisors.
•    Analyze and provide comments on proposed accounting, assurance and ethics standards that are issued for comment by domestic and international standard setters.
•    Participate on special projects pertaining to financial reporting and assurance matters, which may involve interaction with external parties, such as other provincial securities regulators or CPAB.
•    Monitor and evaluate new and evolving trends and developments in financial reporting and assurance, including the activities of national and international standards-setting bodies, and provide information about these trends and developments to other OSC divisions and accounting staff.
•    Communicate staff’s views on important financial reporting and assurance issues through publications and public speaking engagements.

•    Demonstrated ability to research, analyze, and synthesize complex multi-dimensional financial reporting problems issues, and develop practical, well-supported recommendations.

•    Proven ability to build collaborative relationships and effectively engage, influence, and communicate with senior leaders and other internal and external stakeholders.

Reporting to the Chief Technology Officer, the System Governance Specialist plays a critical role in strengthening the organization’s control environment by bridging audit, risk, and technology. This role requires an individual who combines hands-on audit experience with strong technical acumen, enabling them to interpret audit findings, assess control gaps, and drive meaningful remediation actions across systems and platforms. The role is accountable for establishing and operating a cohesive governance function across Information Services & Digital Solutions (ISDS), combining hands-on execution with strategic advisory. The role serves as the central point of integration for audit, risk, and control activities, while translating these inputs into clear, decision-ready insight that informs ISDS leadership prioritization, trade-offs, and operational direction.
While maintaining responsibility for technology governance processes, including risk registers, audit coordination, and reporting, the role elevates governance beyond coordination by identifying systemic risks, challenging assumptions, and providing actionable recommendations that strengthen control effectiveness, improve resilience, and align technology risks with enterprise risk visibility.
This role ensures technology risk is not only well-governed, but meaningfully integrated into enterprise risk visibility, complementing Enterprise Risk Management and Internal Audit while influencing outcomes across both.
Key Duties and Responsibilities
Proactive Risk Assessment and Control Advisory
Provide forward-looking risk insight by identifying emerging technology, operational, and vendor risks and advising leadership on potential impacts and mitigation strategies.
Translate complex risk, audit, and operational data into decisive, outcome-oriented recommendations that shape prioritization, funding, and execution trade-offs.
Advise leadership on risk acceptance, mitigation strategies, and residual exposure during transformation initiatives, major programs, and operational changes.
Challenge existing control environments by identifying systemic weaknesses, root causes, and opportunities for standardization across ISDS.
Drive alignment between ISDS risk practices and enterprise risk frameworks, ensuring technology risks are consistently positioned within enterprise risk discussions.
Analyze audit findings and translate them into clear, actionable control remediation plans.
Proactively advise product managers and business lines on controls that should be embedded into systems and processes to mitigate risk.
Ensure controls are not only documented but effectively implemented within platforms and workflows.
Governance, Risk, and Audit Coordination
Own the evolution of the ISDS Risk Register into a decision-support tool, incorporating trend analysis, systemic risk identification, and prioritization aligned to business impact.
Convert audit findings and assessments into enterprise-relevant themes, addressing root causes rather than isolated issues.
Act as the authoritative interface between ISDS and Audit & Risk, influencing how technology risks are represented, interpreted, and escalated.
Shape enterprise risk reporting by ensuring technology risks are clearly articulated, appropriately prioritized, and connected to broader organizational risk themes.
Prepare consolidated ISDS risk inputs for quarterly and annual organizational risk reporting cycles.
Work closely with audit, risk, and technology teams to interpret audit recommendations and define appropriate technical and operational responses.
Provide specific, practical guidance to engineering and product teams on how to implement control improvements, not just coordinate activities.
Track and report on remediation progress, ensuring clear communication with internal and external auditors.
Develop a strong understanding of OSC’s systems and platforms and how controls operate within them.
Assess system designs and configurations to ensure alignment with control requirements and risk management standards.
Act as a trusted advisor to technical teams, ensuring control requirements are understood and properly embedded in system design and delivery.
Audit Findings Management
Maintain authoritative oversight of all audit and assessment findings impacting ISDS, ensuring completeness, accuracy, and strategic relevance.
Drive management responses that address root causes and lead to sustainable control improvements, not just issue closure.
Ensure executive reporting reflects a clear, accurate, and insight-driven view of audit exposure and progress.
Planning and Timeline Management
Establish and manage a forward-looking ISDS audit and risk roadmap, aligning governance activities with enterprise priorities and decision cycles.
Lead ISDS engagement in SOC and external assessments, ensuring outcomes strengthen control posture and align with strategic governance objectives.
Governance Forums and Reporting
Lead the development of executive-ready ISDS reporting that highlights key risk exposures, trends, trade-offs, mitigations, and required decisions.
Shape leadership forums into decision-oriented discussions focused on prioritization, accountability, business impact, and remediation.
Ensure governance outputs directly influence planning, investment decisions, and performance management across ISDS.
Facilitate governance forums with a strong emphasis on driving outcomes, resolving ambiguity, and enforcing accountability.
Operational Metrics and Reporting Framework
Define and operationalize metrics that provide meaningful insight into risk exposure, control effectiveness, and organizational performance.
Leverage metrics to identify trends, predict emerging issues, and proactively inform leadership actions.
Continuously refine reporting to focus on what matters most, eliminating low-value metrics and emphasizing decision-relevant insights.
Compliance and Audit Readiness
Drive a proactive compliance posture by identifying gaps early and embedding sustainable governance practices.

Promote a collect-once, reuse-many governance model to improve efficiency and consistency across audits and assessments.

title: Practicum Student
employer: Public Health Ontario (Ontario Agency for Health Protection and Promotion)
description:
Practicum Student
Location: Toronto-661 University
Department: Scientist, Third Party Grants
This posting is to fill a current vacancy.
The Role:
The successful applicant will have the opportunity to contribute to two alcohol labelling research studies led by Dr. Erin Hobin. High-quality experimental evidence testing the effectiveness of alcohol labels on consumer outcomes is limited. To address this gap, Dr. Hobin is using novel research methods permitting experimental control in the field to estimate the impacts of alcohol warning labels on consumer knowledge and perceptions of alcohol health risks, and on alcohol use. This research responds to the policy priorities and evidence needs of Canadian and international decision-making bodies, including Health Canada and the World Health Organization. The successful applicant will have the opportunity to contribute to the research processes for two alcohol labelling studies.
The first study is a randomized field experiment to test the effects of different alcohol warning labels on consumer alcohol cognitions and on alcohol use. More than 1500 participants will be recruited from across the 10 provinces, randomized to 1 of 4 alcohol label conditions, and couriered a supply of labels according to their assigned label condition. Participants will be instructed to affix 1 label to all alcohol containers in their home over a 4-week period. Outcomes will be assessed at baseline and at 4 follow-up points using a brief online survey. Self-reported alcohol use will be corroborated using lipid biomarkers. The successful applicant will assist with coordinating the initial study administration planning, materials, and applications.
The second study is a pilot project assessing a standardized protocol for the self-collection of two dried blood spot samples from participants and testing the between-subject variability and inter-day precision of PEth levels as a biomarker of medium-term alcohol exposures as compared to self-reports of alcohol beverage consumption acquired by a series of weekly on-line surveys. Two sets of dried blood spots will be collected by participants over a 4 week period using a commercial dried blood spot collection device.
Please note:
•	This position is only open to students who are currently enrolled in an academic program where the completion of a practicum placement is required.
•	This position is only open to students currently residing in Ontario and attending a Canadian academic institution. Preference will be given to students enrolled in Ontario-based academic institutions.
•	This is a paid placement.
Suggested placement date: January to April 2027
Educational objectives:
• Support the collection, cleaning and management of primary data in one study.

refinement of participant-facing materials.

troubleshooting technical issues.

•
Contribute to status and data reports for funding partners for the research.

• Oral presentation of the projects’ methods and results, delivered to a public health
audience.
Required education and experience:
•
Current enrollment in a Master of Public Health (MPH) program.

• Strong oral and written communication skills.
• Knowledge of SAS or R (statistical software) considered an asset.

experience considered an asset.

description:
Laboratory Attendant 2
Location: PHO Corporate Office & Toronto Laboratory, 661 University Avenue, Toronto, ON
Department: Microbiology and Laboratory Science, Third Party Funding
This posting is to fill a current vacancy.
The Role:
To provide technical laboratory services to the laboratory science and research team to support research project related activities.
Key Responsibilities-
Logs, sorts, labels all specimens submitted for laboratory testing/examination.
Transports samples to testing laboratory as required.
Handles, prepares and processes medical samples (e.g. culture media and reagents) for identification of micro-organisms, reagents and solutions and testing up to the point of result interpretation (e.g. set up of cultures, staining, extraction, loading analyzers).
Handles, prepares, processes and enters data.
Uses automated equipment or manual methods to prepare and aliquot human samples for testing.
Prepares, loads and unloads laboratory analyzers.
Performs inventory management functions including ordering, unpacking and storing of laboratory goods.
Files, stores, discards laboratory samples.
Cleans and maintains laboratory equipment, cleans and disinfects laboratory work areas.
Maintains laboratory stock supplies.
Assists with set-up of quality control and maintenance of stock cultures.
Answers telephone and resolves problems related to samples (e.g., incomplete information, mismatched tests and information, leaking samples).
Performs other duties or projects as assigned.
Knowledge and Skills-
Knowledge of medical terminology and laboratory safety procedures to provide a range of laboratory services in support of operations.
Knowledge of computer systems, familiarity with laboratory information systems, MS office products such as Word and Excel.
Proficient computer skills necessary to work with automated, computer driven equipment.
Education and Experience-
Certification as a Medical Laboratory Technician from a recognized community college program or relevant training and experience.
Attributes and Competencies-
Oral communication skills to exchange information and clarify test requests or discrepancies with other project team members.
Written communication skills to record information into logs/records.
